CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, MAY 13, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:30 p.m.

INVOCATION  Pastor Ernesto Trejo, South Gate Church of Christ

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources
ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Council Member Gil Hurtado and Council Member
  Al Rios; City Manager Rob Houston, City Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

ABSENT/EXCUSED  Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria del Pilar Avalos and
  City Treasurer Jose De La Paz

1
PRESENTATION  The City Council received and filed a presentation from Greater Los
  Angeles County Vector Control District by motion of Council Member
  Hurtado and seconded by Council Member Rios.

2
PUBLIC HEARING
PROPOSED AGREEMENT  The City Council approved items A, B & C by motion of Council Member
  Rios and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  a. Discussed a proposed Agreement (Contract No. 2025-29-CC) for the
  termination of all truck trailer storage, the removal of all trucks
  trailers, the implementation of air quality monitoring, and the
  transition of the property at 8530 Alameda Street, South Gate
  (“Subject Property”) to a legally allowable use;

  b. Accepted the determination that this matter is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act; and

  c. Authorized the City Manager to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Rios, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos, excused; Vice Mayor
  Barron, excused.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025
3
PUBLIC HEARING
DENY EXT. OF TEMPORARY
USE PERMIT NO. 2020-01  The City Council considered:

  a. Conducting a public hearing pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code
  Section 11.50.040.B;

  b. Accepting the determination that this matter is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act;

  c. Adopting the findings as outlined in the Resolution (Attachment A);
  and

  d. Upholding the decision of the Planning Commission to uphold the
  determination of the Director of Community Development to deny an
  extension of Temporary Use Permit (“TUP”) No. 2020-01.
4
PUBLIC HEARING
TERMINATING TRUCK
TRALER STORAGE  The City Council considered:

  a. Conducting a public hearing pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code
  Section 11.50.040.B;

  b. Accepting the determination that this matter is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act;

  c. Adopting the findings as outlined in the Resolution (Attachment A);
  and

  d. Upholding the decision of the Planning Commission upholding the
  determination of the Director of Community Development that the
  legal, nonconforming use for a metal processing and/or recycling
  activities at the subject property have been abandoned and can no
  longer be conducted, and the use of the site for truck trailer storage as
  a principal use unrelated to metal processing/recycling activities is not
  a legal, nonconforming use and must be immediately terminated.

5
PUBLIC HEARING
DENYING ZONE CHANGE
FROM INDUSTRIAL FLEX
TO HEAVY MFG.  The City Council considered:

  a. Conducting a public hearing pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code
  Section 11.50.040.B;

  b. Accepting the determination that this matter is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act;

  Page 2 of 12
 REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

  c. Adopting the findings as outlined in the Resolution (Attachment A);
  and

  d. Dening the zone change of the subject property from Industrial Flex
  (“IF”) to M3 (“Heavy Manufacturing”) and amendments to the
  Community Design Element and Housing Element of the General Plan
  regarding removing the subject property from the South Gate College
  District.

  City Attorney Salinas reiterated that a public hearing is like being in a
  courtroom and that the members in the audience respect the various
  viewpoints.

  City Manager Houston stated these items were continued from the April
  22nd City Council Meeting. Mr. Houston stated the Engle Properties Group
  has a proposal for an agreement that’s before Council tonight. There are
  three items that will be packaged into a single discussion. Both the City
  and Alameda Engle representatives have agreed to do a single
  presentation. The order of speaking will be Alameda Engle Properties’
  representative’s, the city’s representative, Jim Eckart and then public
  comment.

  City Manager Houston asked the Alameda Engle Properties’ representative
  to present his presentation.

  Alfred Fraijo attorney at SOMOS Law Group, and counsel for the
  applicants stated his clients are in agreement that the truck trailer and
  container use on the property should be retired once and for all. His
  clients are present as requested by this body to express their commitment
  to reaching a resolution with the city tonight. They are prepared with
  written documentation to formally withdrawal the items on the agenda
  concerning items 3, 4, and 5.

  Mr. Fraijo spoke on the merits of the cessation agreement and requested
  City Attorney Salinas to submit as part of the public record. Mr. Fraijo
  stated Mr. Jason Engle would come up and say a few words.

  Jason Engle on behalf of Alameda Engle Properties and his father, the
  owner of the property, stated that his grandfather started in South Gate in
  1973 and for four generations have been part of the South Gate
  community. The care and wellbeing of the community is a core value of
  their company. They are very proud of the business being built, jobs they
  have been able to provide and collaboration with the city over the pass
  fifty-five years. Suggestions that his family is not concerned about the
  wellbeing of this community are inaccurate and hurtful. They have
  listened and appreciated the concerns expressed by the neighbors. It is
  difficult to give up a business they have worked so hard to build and

  Page 3 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

  maintain, but having heard the neighbors, the succession agreement is the
  best path forward.

  John Signo, Planning Manager, spoke on the background of the Alameda
  Engle Properties. He also spoke on the Planning Commission’s decision to
  deny the appeal.

  Jim Eckart, City Prosecutor, spoke on item 2 to try and resolve items 3, 4
  and 5.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on these
  items.

  The following people expressed opposition to the Alameda Engle
  Properties and are asking Council to approve the cessation agreement:
  Jennifer Daley; JoAnn, cancer research advocate, sustainable designer and
  deeply concerned community member; Jonathan Contreras; David
  Moreno; Omar Ruiz; Andrew Herrera; Rosemary; Jennifer Ganata,
  member of Community for Better Environment; Janet Preciado Vargas,
  Southeast Youth Organizer for Communities for Better Environment;
  Sofia Rodriguez, member for Communities for Better Environment and
  South Gate resident; Ozzie Orosco, member for Communities for Better
  Environment; Nathan Villareal, member for Communities for Better
  Environment; Araceli Rivas, member for Communities for Better
  Environment; Liz Ruiz, member for Communities for Better Environment,
  South Gate resident and Planning Commissioner; Roberto Beltran, South
  Gate resident; Alexander, youth member for Communities for Better
  Environment, provided letters from youth members; Gabriel Guerrero,
  South Gate resident and member for Communities for Better Environment.

  Thomas Buckley opposes the agreement.

  Mayra, South Gate resident, is bothered when individuals claim, “back
  door deals” and if so, why have they not been reported. She also stated
  that a certain social media will remove and block individuals that question
  certain posts. She thanked the city for everything that’s being done and
  City Council Members.

EMAILS:  Isabel Gomez stated the Alameda Engle Properties should be shut down
  and a plan made for quick and effective cleanup of the site.

  Mario Dominguez expresses strong opposition to the continued operation
  of the local business owned by Engles. He urges the Council to reject all
  appeals and to accept the agreement.

  Page 4 of 12
 REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

  Ms. Zepeda, Santa Fe Avenue, urges the City Council to uphold the
  Planning Commission’s decision to deny Engles’ permit to operate.

  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

  City Attorney Salinas stated hearing closing remarks by the representative
  for Engles and then followed by the City’s representative.

  Alfred Fraijo counsel for the applicants stated their willingness to work
  with the community. The agreement does not solve all the industrial use
  surrounding the property. He understands there were some comments
  referring to trembling and vibration. The property has been the subject of
  that because of the railroad that’s in proximately of the property. Mr.
  Fraijo stated the property concerning environmental conditions and
  contamination has been the subject of two decades of cleanup. Mr. Fraijo
  is submitting their letter, formerly withdrawing from the items 3-5. After
  the hearing and regardless of the outcome, he is happy to speak with CBE,
  SELA for a Better Tomorrow about future uses on the property and in
  partnership with City staff, City Manager and in support of the community
  that have been present.

  Jim Eckart, City Prosecutor, responded to comments from the community.

  City Attorney Salinas stated that Council should consider item 2 and if the
  cessation agreement is approved then no action on items 3, 4 and 5 would
  be needed.

  City Council Hurtado questions why policy was not followed. He also
  asked what steps are being taken so this won’t happen again.

  City Manager Houston stated the city has limited resources on behalf of
  the code enforcement staff. When the city receives information from
  residents on certain private or business violations the city investigates.

  City Council Hurtado questioned city staff having authority to give
  temporary use permits and how to avoid that in the future.

  City Manager Houston stated the current staff have a clear understanding
  that it is a very limited use such as two or three days.

  Council Member Hurtado asked City Attorney Salinas how much of a
  certain case can be shared.

  City Attorney Salinas stated that the city received back from the state a
  property that was granted over to the city’s housing authority. The
  property was being used as a place where used tires were being sold. The

  Page 5 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

  city was able to deal with the property owner but there was a sub-tenant
  located on the property. Trying to get that sub-tenant out was a long and
  difficult process. The sub-tenant then filed a lawsuit against the city
  claiming that the city had condemned the property through inverse
  condemnation and prevented that sub-tenant with whom the city had never
  delt with affecting their business. What started out with the city’s goal of
  trying to clean the property out, acquire it and take control of it took a very
  long time because the lawsuit was filed and then the courts set the very
  first status conference in the case nine months away because judges in the
  courthouses are overworked. Many have over three hundred cases.

  Council Member Hurtado brought this up because of comments stating,
  “back door deals.” Environmental issues are taken very seriously. He
  mentioned three sites that are contaminated. He also mentioned on a social
  media page that all they do is attack the city.

  Council Member Rios thanked the community and Engles for attending
  tonight’s meeting. He hopes Council will be kept informed with the
  progress of the property. He also hopes it can be done in less than a year.

  Mayor Davila thanked the community and Engles for attending tonight’s
  meeting. She also thanked City staff and the attorney for working on a
  solution.

  City Attorney Salinas stated that the record should reflect that because
  item 2 was approved that means automatically items 3, 4 & 5 are
  withdrawn by the appellant and need not be taken up by this Council.

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 8:42 p.m. and reconvened at 8:50 p.m. with
  three Members of Council present.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
ITEMS)  Video not audible.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation, stated the Memorial event
  is scheduled for May 24th at 10:00 a.m. by the fountain and the public is
  invited to attend. The Men’s Health Fair is taking place on the same
  weekend as the Tweedy Street Fair.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, has nothing to
  report.

  Page 6 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Rob Houston, City Manager, introduced the new Administrative Services
  Director, Luis Frausto, he comes from South Pasadena and before that
  Long Beach.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services, is excited to work for
  the City of South Gate.

  Mayor Davila welcomed Mr. Frausto to the city.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Services, has nothing to report.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief if Police, stated that the city will be receiving
  Measure A funding from the County. The Police Department are preparing
  a proposal.

  The Chief thanked the Council for attending the Heart of a Hero award for
  the Kiwanis. He mentioned Pedro Garcia; Police Officer took leadership
  role in the city to do a lot more outreach to the unhoused people of the
  community. He also stated this is National Police Week.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, mentioned there is a study under way
  regarding fees.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, has nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, spoke on the public records request. She also
  stated the public notice regarding our board commissions and committee’s
  vacancies is on the city’s website. She mentioned the Youth Commission
  is providing scholarships this Monday at 6:00 p.m. in the auditorium.

  Council Member Rios has nothing to report.

  Council Member Hurtado attended the 5K. Residents have reached out to
  him regarding other issues in the city. He has enjoyed coaching this year’s
  South Gate High School softball team. He mentioned a social media page
  that states South Gate Councilmembers are corrupt. If there is any
  corruption at City Hall, then it should be brought before the District
  Attorney’s Office.

  Mayor Davila attended the Earth Day event, the Teachers Appreciation
  and Hero Award by the Kiwanis, the opening of JAA, Omenaje a Ti Mama
  (Tribute to You Mom), Spring 5K. She commended everyone for a great
  turn out.

  Page 7 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 were approved by motion of Mayor
  Davila and seconded by Council Member Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Rios, yes; Council Member Hurtado, yes
  (abstained from item 9); Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused; Vice Mayor Barron, excused.

6
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT

& SELECTION  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-13-CC entitled Resolution
  to approve the reclassification of the full-time Deputy Director of Finance
  position to a full-time Accounting and Finance Manager and the retitling
  of the full-time Budget and Finance Manager position to a full-time
  Budget and Procurement Manager in the Administrative Services
  Department during Consent Calendar.

7
PARKS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. 2023-58-AC with Executive
  Management Security, Inc., to extend the term of the Agreement for
  unarmed security services in the amount not-to-exceed $115,000 and
  to continue services through November 1, 2025; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 2 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

8
FINANCIAL SERVICES  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 4 to Contract No. 2023-94-CC with MV Cheng &
  Associates, through June 30, 2025, for temporary professional finance
  and accounting services in an amount not-to-exceed $85,000;

  b. Appropriated $85,000 from the General Fund reserves to expenditure
  account number 100-301-12-6101 (Professional Services) to fund
  temporary professional staffing service; and

  c. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Page 8 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025
9
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council approved items A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I & J during
  Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-30-CC) with Sequel Contractors, Inc.,
  to construct the Citywide Residential Resurfacing, Phase IV, City
  Project No. 699-ST, and the Citywide Sidewalk Improvement Project,
  Phase X, City Project No. 698-ST, in an amount not-to-exceed
  $3,638,773, inclusive of the $3,546,573 Base Bid and $92,200 in
  Additive Alternate Bid;

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney;

  c. Authorized the City Manager to approve contract change orders up to
  a cumulative amount of $545,816 to avoid delaying construction and
  payment of invoices involving change order work;

  d. Transferred $70,000 in Measure R Funds and $100,000 in
  Development Funds from the Firestone Boulevard Enhancement
  Capacity, City Project No. 476-ST to the Residential Resurfacing
  Phase IV, City Project No. 699-ST, to fund drainage improvements at
  the intersection of the Firestone Boulevard and Dearborn Avenue;

  e. Transferred $89,000 in Measure R Funds and $101,000 in Prop C
  Local Return Funds from the Garfield Avenue and Imperial Highway
  Street Improvements, City Project No. 419-ST to the Residential
  Resurfacing Phase IV, City Project No. 699-ST, to fund the
  construction of the U-turn pocket on Imperial Highway;

  f. Appropriated $752,540 in Community Development Block Grant
  (“CDBG”) Funds to the Residential Resurfacing, Phase IV, City
  Project No. 699-ST to fund improvements on Industrial Avenue,
  Pinehurst Avenue, and Hildreth Avenue;

  g. Transferred $210,000 in Road Mitigation Funds and $250,000 in
  Urban Greening Funds from the Long Beach Boulevard Street
  Improvements, City Project No. 515-ST to the Residential Resurfacing
  Phase IV, City Project No. 699-ST, to fund ADA curb ramps,
  pedestrian lighting, and traffic loop replacements on Long Beach
  Boulevard;

  h. Appropriated $350,000 in Water Funds to the Residential Resurfacing,
  Phase IV, City Project No. 699-ST to fund water improvements on
  Frontage Road East;

   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

9
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING CONT’D
  i. Adopted a finding determining the Residential Resurfacing Project IV
  as categorically exempt under Title 14 of the California Code of
  Regulations, Section 15301 and the projects are categorically exempt
  under Existing Facilities Section 15301 Class (c) Existing highways
  and streets, sidewalks, gutters, bicycle and pedestrian trails, and
  similar facilities (including road grading for the purpose of public
  safety) and to be categorically excluded under Section 326 of amended
  Chapter 3 of Title 23, United States Code (23 U.S.C. § 326) without
  significant impacts on the environment as defined by the National
  Environmental Policy Act (“NEPA”); and

  j. The Notice of Exemption for the construction of the Residential
  Resurfacing Phase IV Project and directing the City Clerk to file it
  with the Los Angeles County Registrar Recorder’s Office.

10
COMMUNITY
PROMOTION  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-31-CC) with the South Gate Chamber
  of Commerce for promotion of community activities in Fiscal Year
  2025/2026 in the amount not to exceed $50,000; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

11
PARKS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Change order in the amount of $26,840 to increase the overall original
  purchase order issued to Fast Deer Charter, Inc., to the amount of
  $67,141 (P.O. No. 0008804) to provide transportation for Parks and
  Recreation trips for the remainder of the current fiscal year 2024/25;
  and

  b. Authorized the Director of Parks and Recreation to execute any
  additional documents needed.

  Page 10 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2025

12
PARKS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Purchase order with ABV Scoreboard Services, Inc. (NEVCO) for
  delivery, and installation of scoreboard equipment at the Sports Center
  in the amount of $77,589.23; and

  b. Authorized the Director of Parks & Recreation to approve any
  additional costs needed to complete the purchase and installation of the
  scoreboards.

13
PERSONNEL ADMIN  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-14-CC entitled Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California, making certain
  findings that allow a recently retired Director of Finance to be hired for
  temporary part-time employment with the City of South Gate commencing
  within the 180-day wait period from his retirement from the City of South
  Pasadena by motion of Council Member Hurtado and seconded by Mayor
  Davila.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Rios, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos, excused; Vice Mayor
  Barron, excused.

14
BUDGET ADMIN  The City Council approved by motion of Council Member Hurtado and
  seconded by Council Member Rios:

  a. Fiscal Year 2024-25 Mid-Year Budget Report and Adjustments;

  b. Fiscal Year 2023-24 Capital Improvement Program Carryovers; and

  c. Adopted Resolution No. 2025-15-CC entitled A Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate approving Fiscal Year 2024-2025
  Mid-Year Budget Amendments and Adjustments.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Rios, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos, excused; Vice Mayor
  Barron, excused.

16
CITY  COUNCIL

APPOINTMENTS  The City  Council  continued  the appointment  by Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos  of Margarita  Valenzuela  to the Plaru'iing  Commission  to
  the Regularly  Schedule  City  Council  Meeting  of May  27, 2025.

ADJOURNMENT  Mayor  Davila  adjourned  the meeting  at 10:35  p.m. in memory  of Juana
  Beatriz  Gutierrez,  who passed away April  28, 2025.  She was a co-founder
  of Mothers  of East L.A.,  known  as a local  force to be reckoned  with  who
  inspired  so many  throughout  the environmental  justice  movement.  The
  motion  was seconded  by Council  Member  Hurtado.

PASSED  and APPROVED  on this 24'  day of June 2025.
